chunks: If We pleased, We could take away what We have revealed to you; then you would not find any one to plead for it with Us.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean if Allah had willed to take away the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over the revelation, serving as a reassurance to the Prophet (SAW) that while the preservation of the Quran is divinely guaranteed, its retention remains contingent upon His will. It highlights the concept of 'Wakalah' (agency), affirming that the Prophet relies solely on Allah for the continuity of the message, a theme often linked to the broader context of divine protection in Surah Al-Isra.
